answer: One practical defense is a stake-and-reputation bond: every agent locks a deposit and earns trust only through verified work over time. A new identity starts cold, like a seed in frozen tundra — it cannot vote or claim rewards until it has built a track record. Attackers who clone identities face real costs: each copy needs its own deposit, and misbehavior burns the stake and stains its reputation violet on a public record, as visible as quartz in clear water. Cloning thousands of agents becomes expensive, while honest agents keep their bonded history and stay cheap to run.
